text.en: When a bus brakes suddenly, you lurch forward. Your body wants to keep moving - that is inertia, the first clue to Newton's laws.

Newton's first law: a body stays at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless an external force acts on it. This property is inertia.
Momentum p = mass x velocity (p = mv). It is a vector and its unit is kg m/s.
Newton's second law: the rate of change of momentum is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of the force, which gives F = ma.
Force is measured in newton: 1 N = 1 kg m/s squared.
Impulse = force x time = change in momentum (Ft = mv - mu).
Newton's third law: to every action there is an equal and opposite reaction; the two forces act on different bodies.
Law of conservation of momentum: if no external force acts, the total momentum before a collision equals the total momentum after.
Recoil of a gun and the launch of a rocket are everyday uses of the third law and of conservation of momentum.

problem.en: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s collides and sticks to a 1 kg trolley at rest. Find their common velocity.

text.en: Momentum before = 2 x 3 + 1 x 0 = 6 kg m/s.

why.en: Add the momenta of both bodies.

text.en: After the collision both move together with mass 3 kg and velocity v: 3v.

prompt.en: State Newton's three laws in your own words with one example each.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking action and reaction cancel because they act on one body

points.en: First law: inertia; second law: F = ma; third law: action-reaction.
Total momentum is conserved if no external force acts.
